thingsToDo.title: Bryce Canyon National Park
thingsToDo.description: Bryce Canyon National Park is a national park in Bryce Canyon City, Utah. Bryce Canyon National Park in southern Utah protects high-elevation amphitheaters filled with hoodoos carved from the Claron Formation. It was designated a national monument in 1923 and a national park in 1928. The park spans the Paunsaugunt Plateau and is a central gateway landscape for Bryce Canyon City tourism, geology interpretation, and year-round scenic visitation.

thingsToDo.title: Bryce Amphitheater
thingsToDo.description: Bryce Amphitheater is a natural amphitheater in Bryce Canyon City, Utah. Bryce Amphitheater is the best-known natural amphitheater in Bryce Canyon National Park and contains dense concentrations of hoodoos shaped by frost weathering and erosion. Major viewpoints, including Sunrise Point and Sunset Point, overlook this basin. The amphitheater defines the park’s visual identity and concentrates trail access, ranger interpretation, and visitor circulation near Bryce Canyon City.

thingsToDo.title: Sunrise Point
thingsToDo.description: Sunrise Point is a viewpoint in Bryce Canyon City, Utah. Sunrise Point is a primary overlook on the Bryce Amphitheater rim in Bryce Canyon National Park. It gives direct views of hoodoo fields including landmarks such as Boat Mesa and the Sinking Ship formation. The viewpoint connects to the Rim Trail and Queen’s Garden Trail, making it a key orientation area for day visitors entering from Bryce Canyon City.

thingsToDo.title: Sunset Point
thingsToDo.description: Sunset Point is a viewpoint in Bryce Canyon City, Utah. Sunset Point is a major Bryce Canyon National Park overlook facing the Bryce Amphitheater and the Thor’s Hammer hoodoo formation. It links directly to the Navajo Loop and Rim Trail corridor and is one of the park’s busiest trailheads. Its high rim location provides broad geologic views that frame Bryce Canyon City’s role as the park’s access community.

thingsToDo.title: Ruby's Inn
thingsToDo.description: Ruby's Inn is a historic resort complex in Bryce Canyon City, Utah. Ruby’s Inn is a long-running lodging and services complex at Bryce Canyon City founded by Reuben C. Syrett in the early twentieth century. It expanded alongside Bryce Canyon’s growth from monument status to national park designation. Ruby's Inn is one of the best-known public landmarks linked to travel patterns around Bryce Canyon City.

faq.a: Two to three days is enough for core Bryce Canyon City highlights plus one or two local experiences.
